question.text: Fund PPI, a Category III AIF, subscribes to Pre-IPO shares of Company ABC at INR 120/share before the IPO at INR 130/share. Per the Pre-IPO Strategy discussion in Chapter 11 of the workbook (which references the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018), the Pre-IPO shares held by institutional investors including AIFs are subject to:

answer.text: No lock-in since AIFs are exempt institutional investors
A 3-year lock-in from the date of Pre-IPO allotment, regardless of IPO timing
A lock-in period from the date of listing of the shares through the IPO
Lock-in only if the AIF receives more than 10% of the IPO size

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 11.2.4.3 (Pre-IPO Strategy) of the workbook, institutional investors including AIFs subscribing to Pre-IPO shares or QIP are subject to a lock-in period from the date of listing of such shares through the IPO. The lock-in clock starts on listing, not on Pre-IPO allotment, under the Chapter 11 discussion which is the source the stem is anchored to. The Trap: Option A is wrong because AIFs are not exempt; no such carve-out exists. Option B invents an allotment-date trigger. Option D invents a size threshold that does not exist in the Chapter 11 passage. Note: The original stem referred broadly to "the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018", which conflicts with later ICDR material (pp. 553-554) describing a 6-month/1-year lock-in from allotment for Category II/III AIFs holding unlisted shares. The stem has been narrowed to the Chapter 11 Pre-IPO Strategy passage so the keyed answer is unambiguously supported. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 283-284.
